Photograph: Natxo Frances/EPA Weather tracker Europe weather Analysis Severe flooding in eastern Spain and UK hit by first named storm of winter Megan Davies, Claire Jones and Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk Storm Adam brings torrential rain to Valencia, Alicante and Balearic Islands, as Storm Austen strikes England and Wales Fri 23 Oct 2026 04.16 EDT Last modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 06.29 EDT Share Storm Adam brought torrential rain to eastern Spain earlier this week. In Pego, Alicante, 632mm fell in 36 hours, with 430mm of this falling in just six hours, while the Valencian town of Olivia received 600mm in 24 hours. The severe flooding led 145 municipalities across Valencia and Alicante to impose a temporary lockdown on about 850,000 people on Monday. At least five people have died, 500 have been rescued and 2,100 evacuated. The storm also affected the Balearic Islands, with more than 130 incidents recorded in Ibiza including standing water at the airport causing some flights to be diverted or suspended. Although the worst of the storm has passed and conditions are improving across Valencia and Alicante, local disruption is expected to continue. The first named storm of the winter for the UK is tracking through the Channel. Storm Austen is bringing damaging winds not only to south-west England and Wales, but south-west Ireland and northern France. Gusts are expected to be around 50-60mph, but some exposed north-western coasts of France could experience winds of up to 80-90mph. View image in fullscreen A car is surrounded by fallen branches in Falmouth, England, after Storm Austen made landfall. Photograph: Hugh R Hastings/Getty Images Following quickly on from Storm Austen is another deep low-pressure system, Storm Boelo, which is expected to track across northern Scotland on Saturday into Sunday. Much of the UK and Ireland will experience very unsettled conditions with further damaging winds, and heavy and prolonged rain. Western Scotland will face the strongest gusts, but the rest of the UK and Ireland can expect 40-55mph winds. Western parts of Ireland will experience 50-60mph winds with up to 70-80mph in exposed parts of north-west Ireland, similar to western Scotland. Again, heavy rain associated with Storm Boelo will reach 10-20mm, with as much as 30-60mm in western parts of Ireland, Wales and south-west England. This, on top of the rainfall from Storm Austen, will increase the risk of flooding. Super Typhoon Champi is heading towards China and Japan over the weekend after passing north-eastern Taiwan on Friday. It has weakened since Wednesday, but is still a significant typhoon with the equivalent strength of a category 5 hurricane, producing 185mph gusts and sustained winds of 121 mph. After torrential rain from the typhoon this week, up to 900mm of rain is forecast to fall in the mountainous regions of northern and eastern Taiwan from Tuesday to Saturday. As a result, there are school closures, cancelled flights and six-metre waves, with damage expected over the next few days. https://aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/latvia-than.text: Türkiye Europe Latvia thanks Türkiye for contribution to airspace protection 'I thank Türkiye for its responsiveness and operational action, providing a significant contribution to strengthening the security of Latvian airspace,' defense minister says Ilayda Cakirtekin 10 October 2026 • Update : 10 October 2026 ISTANBUL Latvian Defense Minister Raivis Melnis thanked Türkiye on Friday for its contribution to strengthening the defense of the country's airspace. "I thank Türkiye for its responsiveness and operational action, providing a significant contribution to strengthening the security of Latvian airspace," Melnis said in a statement issued by the Defense Ministry. The statement came after Melnis met with a Turkish Air Force unit at the National Armed Forces military base in Lielvarde. "The presence of Turkish fighter jets in Lielvarde demonstrates NATO's ability to respond quickly and effectively move forces where they are needed," he said. Melnis further stressed the need for close cooperation between allies, mutual trust, and readiness to act together for the security of Latvia and the entire eastern flank of NATO. The statement noted that Turkish Air Force F-16 fighters were temporarily stationed in Latvia to support NATO Integrated Air and Missile Defense activities.
